reason:
An owner-local repository policy selects PR review for every importance level without changing the signed assessment.
Readiness and merge require actual current-head PR review, and publication honors the PR pause without inserting suppression.
Keep earlier CLI findings when switching routes and record the actual route for high assessments already reviewed through PR.
Repository owners link open issues to existing PRs through live numeric owner and repository-network checks.
The operation preserves the original body prefix and review metadata, sends one body-only update, and checks its acknowledgement and readback.
Unknown write outcomes stop without retrying, and unobserved concurrent edits remain an external assumption.
Normal preparation and creation use the owner's open stack tip.
One stack counts as one work unit, and each declared independent PR adds one unit.
Independent declarations bind the owner-local reason to the repository identities, login, branch, issue, starting history, and created PR number.
The reason stays out of the public PR body.
Creation checks dependencies on every PR outside the selected parent chain, including for a new stack member.
It reports and skips PRs opened by bots and stale PRs that already conflict with their own base.
For every remaining PR, shared commits and conflicts from an in-memory merge of overlapping heads require a stack or resolution before extending the open stack.
Git execution failures stop creation, and no caller override bypasses the dependency decision.
Merge commands fetch the verified heads, carry signed assessments only across unchanged diffs and identities, and wait for running checks.
Active merge queue rules select queue admission, whose eventual result remains bound to the verified heads.
Every repository uses the owner's shared gh-stack installation at its pinned version.
Persisted prose and replies keep one sentence per line in English and Japanese.
Split long sentences into shorter ones when a channel limits line length.
The shell guard checks available GitHub publication bodies with the matching prose channel.
Static word decoding preserves argument bytes, and unavailable or ambiguous inputs block the command.
Structured name-and-email metadata keeps its spelling without making an identity claim.
